item.title: Aso Caldera & Daikanbō Viewpoint — Guide
item.description: The Aso caldera, in the heart of Aso-Kujū National Park, is one of the largest volcanic calderas in the world — a vast basin some 25 km across, ringed by mountains, holding a green landscape of towns, rice fields and grasslands within its walls. Touring it by car is one of the great scenic drives of Kyushu. The classic viewpoint is Daikanbō, a lookout on the caldera’s northern rim offering a jaw-dropping panorama over the entire basin, the central volcanic peaks and the outer rim — from here the row of central cones is said to resemble a ‘sleeping Buddha’ reclining on the plain.
